### Welcome to ANSR

An R package to query ANSIS and massage the responses into various useful formats.

The [Australian National Soil Information System](https://ansis.net/) (ANSIS) brings together a range of publicly available soil profile data sets from across Australia. It delivers data in the form of a standardised JSON Schema preserving complex relationships within the data. This JSON data can be daunting to untangle.

ANSR does all the hard work of querying ANSIS and parsing the JSON response data into simpler formats - mainly CSV files.

### About ANSIS

ANSIS provides access to nationally consistent, standardised soil data through an access control, trusted mechanism – ANSIS is the new place to find readily useable soil data and information. Users of ANSIS can:

- Discover, filter, access and view relevant soil data

- Download soil data in a standard format for use in modelling or analysis

- Use an Application Programming Interface (API) to connect soil data through ANSIS into your own system or application

- Easily connect to the latest available soil data using your preferred GIS and modelling applications.

ANSIS allows the discovery of soil data from multiple providers, which enables ANSIS users to make better informed decisions. With improved access to soil data and information ANSIS provides a foundational information infrastructure to support sustainable soil management for future generations.

### Getting Started with ANSR

The ANSR package requires you to have an ANSIS account and be logged into it. If you don't have an ANSIS account got to the ANSIS website to create one.

<https://portal.ansis.net/>

Once you have created your ANSIS account you need to keep these details somewhere to supply to the ANSR package. A convenient way to store the details and keep them from being shared accidentally is to create an entry in your "R.environ" file in your home directory on your local machine as per below.

[ANSISUser='YourANSISUserName']{style="color: #DB7107;"}

[ANSISPassword='YourANSISPassword']{style="color: #DB7107;"}

<BR> Then you can retrieve the values into your current session using

[username \<- Sys.getenv("ANSISUser")]{style="color: #DB7107;"}

[password \<- Sys.getenv("ANSISPassword")]{style="color: #DB7107;"}

<BR> Or you can just hard code them into this script.

[username = 'YourANSISUserName']{style="color: #DB7107;"} [password = 'YourANSISPassword']{style="color: #DB7107;"}

<BR> Now we need to Authenticate with the ANSIS API using the apiAuthoriseMe() function. This function also sSets up a directory where all of the ANSIS data downloads will be written automatically

[DataStorePath = 'c:/temp/ansis']{style="color: #DB7107;"}

[apiAuthoriseMe(username = username, password = password, DataStorePath = DataStorePath)]{style="color: #DB7107;"}

### <BR> The ANSIS Query Workflow 

OK you are good to go. All ANSIS data requests via the ANSIS API have a similar workflow

1 - Generate an ANSIS query JSON object

2 - Send this request to the API

3 - Check with the API to determine when the query has finished processing on the ANSIS server

4 - Download the JSON files generated by the query and ad them to a zip file - one per query

5 - Parse these JSON files into a flat file (csv) structure

The ANSR package provides functions to undertake all of these steps individually or you can use a wrapper function

to run all of these steps in sequence.

4.1 Run the wrapper function below to undertake the query process in one command.

AnsisDataObject \<- apiGetANSISData(queryName='ANSISDemo', description = "This is a description of the purpose of the query", minx=147, maxx=151, miny=-29, maxy=-25, provider = 'CSIRO', ansisProperties=c('Concentration of organic Carbon', 'pH', 'Texture'), overwrite=T, parseAll = F, verbose=T, viewSummaries=T)

This function returns a list of ANSIS data and some summary info

####See the package help for details about the function parameters
